notes: kb/Work PB5175 landed. §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR6: 'The currency symbol must be the leftmost character position to be counted in the size of the item except that it can be preceded by either a '+' or a '-' symbol.' PictureComposition.Precedence reads the edition: below 2002 a fixed currency symbol takes the one role the 1985 chart (§1985:VI.5.9.6) gives it, PicRole.CurrencyLeading; the trailing role (§2002:13.16.38.2 SR23, §2023:13.18.40.3 SR26) is offered from 2002. So PIC 999$, +999$ and 999$CR are refused at 85 (COBOL1935, whose 85 message names the 1985 chart) and accepted from 2002. Validate refuses a second fixed currency or sign symbol and two kinds of sign symbol (COBOL1934); the walk refuses CR or DB anywhere but last and '+' or '-' anywhere but first or last and admits +$999 and -$999; CobolEdit.Render places each insertion character. Witnesses: 1985-GR-VI_5_9_5-6 (+999, -999, $999CR, $999DB), pb5175-trailing-currency-85 and pb5175-trailing-currency-cr-85 (refused at 85), pb5175-trailing-currency (accepted from 2002).

next.reason: 1985: 'The currency symbol must be the leftmost character position ... except that it can be preceded by either a '+' or a '-''. §2023:13.18.40.3 SR26 also allows it as 'the rightmost symbol in character-string-1, optionally followed by one of the symbols '+', '-', 'CR', or 'DB'', so PIC 999$ and 999$CR, refused in 1985, are accepted (looser). The one-symbol limits (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR23, SR24), sign position (§2023:13.18.40.3 SR25), CR/DB size (§2023:13.18.40.4 GR14) and the result table (§2023:13.18.40.5 GR5) are unchanged.
